messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <psharma@clinexhealth.com>, Jordan Li <jordan.li@clinexhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying transient logs + keystore residency carveout

Hi Priya / Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Short recap of the ask and what we discussed so we’re aligned before legal takes a pass:

- Ask: Clinex wants Redwood to support a carveout where conversational inputs that include PHI/PII are not persisted to long-term disk in our multi-tenant hosted environment. Specifically: 0-day retention for full text plus a separate keystore to hold per-customer encryption keys that must be resident in a US-only HSM.
- Constraints we heard: clinical transcripts may contain patient identifiers; auditability and SOC2 evidence are required for the exception; you need a way to prove deletion/ephemeral handling for compliance.
- What Redwood can provisionally offer: transient in-memory processing with an optional short-lived log (7 days) for troubleshooting, plus a customer-dedicated keystore option (bring-your-own-key or Redwood-managed HSM in a US region). We flagged that the keystore residency + HSM requirement will likely push the engagement toward Dedicated or Private deployment for the SLA/evidence needs.

Open items / next steps we agreed on:
1) Clinex to share a short list of exact artifacts you need as evidence (SOC2 sections, sample retention attestation language, any required log formats).
2) Redwood to produce a 1-page technical diagram showing: transient path, what is logged (if anything), where KV/keystore lives, and how deletion/TTL is enforced — target by EOD Thu (2027-05-06).
3) Legal to propose redline language for the retention carveout (we can start with a targeted addendum) — we asked for a first pass within 3 business days.
4) We also discussed a quick pilot: we can enable a 7-day short-log pilot scoped to a single model and single route; pilot success criteria: no commuter-visible PII in stored logs and demonstrable deletion artifacts.

Attachments: draft checklist and a short sketch of the runtime flow (I’ll attach the diagram in a follow-up).

If I missed anything or you want different wording for legal, tell me and I’ll update.

Best,
Ben

Thanks Ben — clear recap and really appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Evidence: Clinex needs an attestation that the stored logs (if any) are rotated and deleted and that we receive a deletion token/assertion showing job id + timestamp. SOC2 Appendix A sections we care about are: logging/monitoring and change control. I’ll paste the exact clause in my next email.
- Pilot: 7 days is fine as long as we get the deletion token at the end. We’re OK with the pilot running on a dedicated route but not full Dedicated infra yet.
- Keystore residency: must be US-only; we prefer customer-managed keys in an HSM we control. Is BYOK to Redwood-managed HSM supported today or would we need Private?

Also looping Jordan — he’s our infra lead and will want to review the diagram and any HSM procedures.

Subject: Internal: quick ops/legal flags on Clinex keystore ask

Ben / Steph —

Quick internal note after reading Priya’s reply:
- BYOK into customer-controlled HSM is something we can support but not on the multi-tenant hosted tier today. That flows into our recommendation that Clinex either: (a) take Redwood Dedicated with a customer-specific keystore on a dedicated subnet, or (b) accept Redwood Private where their HSM / KMS is colocated.
- If Clinex absolutely needs hosted + BYOK we can discuss guarded bridge patterns (encrypted envelope keys held by Redwood but wrapped by customer key) — this will carry additional compliance scrutiny and involves an architecture review.
- For the deletion token: runtime can emit a signed deletion receipt (job id, TTL start, TTL end, SHA256 of removed artifact id) — ops can produce a scripted evidence bundle for audits, but legal will want explicit language about what we attest to.

I’ll draft the technical diagram Ben requested and include two options annotated (Hosted+envelope flow vs Dedicated/Private). Target: Thu EOD.

Rishi

Priya —

Thanks for the prompt reply and for committing to the SOC2 clause — that helps a lot. Quick update from our side:

- Attached: I’ve uploaded the initial diagram and the evidence checklist to the shared Drive (link below). The diagram contains two candidate flows (hosted envelope pattern + dedicated-keystore pattern) and highlights what we can meaningfully attest to.
- Pilot plan: Redwood will stand up the pilot on a scoped route. We will provide weekly logs during the pilot and a signed deletion token at the end of the 7-day window. If Clinex wants the deletion token after each rotation, we can automate that as part of the pilot scope.
- Keystore: BYOK into your HSM is supported in Private; for Hosted we can do envelope-wrapping where your key wraps an envelope key stored on our side — this reduces your control surface but is sometimes acceptable. Rishi will include both options on the diagram.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Share Drive with diagram + checklist (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cClinex-Docs) — DONE.
2) Rishi to post the technical diagram and short decision table by EOD today.
3) Stephanie to coordinate with Legal for a narrow retention carveout addendum template (she’ll send the first redline).
4) Priya to confirm pilot scope and desired deletion token cadence.

If that looks right we can schedule a 30-minute alignment call next week to walk lawyers through the flows.

Best,
Ben
